paragraph: The single-family market is the story in Northvale, with 19 sales over six months at a median of $770,000, and the typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial or split-level with two full baths. Sale prices ran from $535,000 to $1,490,000, so the median is the number to anchor on. A median of 16 days on market with nearly 58 percent of homes closing above asking tells you well-priced houses are moving, but a sale-to-list ratio right at 1.00 says this is competitive rather than frenzied. Expect competition on the good ones and room to negotiate on the rest. Condos and townhouses are a much smaller slice at 6 sales and a median of $655,000, mostly two-bedroom units with a bath and a half, sitting a bit longer at 33 days and selling right at list. Monthly counts here are too thin to read as a trend, so treat the July jump in the single-family median as mix rather than a price move. If you're choosing between tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance setup of a condo.
